Order Management Automation · Zapier

Online Store: End-to-End Order Management Automation

A customer fills in an order form. From that moment, six connected Zaps check the stock, log the order, alert the team, create and email an invoice, track the order on a Trello board and keep the customer updated, so nobody has to do it by hand.

GmailDocs & Drive
The idea

How it works

Every order starts in one form and ends as one row in a Google Sheet. The Main Zap logs the order and checks the stock. If the item is available, it takes one off the stock, tells the team on Slack, then calls two Sub-Zaps: one creates and emails the invoice, the other puts a card on the right Trello list. After that, staff move the card, and each move starts the Zap that updates the sheet and emails the customer.

The impact

What this does for the store

The goal was to take the repetitive parts of running an online store off the owner's plate, and make sure no order, invoice or customer update gets forgotten.

01No manual order entryEvery order is logged, numbered and invoiced from the form, so there is nothing to retype.
02Stock that stays accurateOrders lower the stock and cancellations put it back, and out of stock items never get sold.
03Customers kept in the loopAn email goes out when an order is received, processed, delivered or cancelled, with no one writing them.
A note on resultsThis is a mock-up store built to demonstrate the system, so no performance figures are claimed here. Numbers such as time saved can only be measured once it runs with real orders.
The key idea

One order, one row

Every order becomes a row in the Orders tab, with its own invoice number and a colour coded status. The stock lives in the Inventory tab. The Zaps read and write both tabs, so the numbers always match what really happened.

Why it mattersThe sheet is the single source of truth. A new order lowers the stock, a cancelled order puts it back, and every status change is written to the same row. Nobody has to retype an order or recount the shelves.
Step 1 · The order form

A short form that asks for exactly what the system needs

The customer picks a category, then a product with its price, then a size. They add a note and choose a delivery date. Dropdowns and required fields keep the data clean from the very first click, so the Zaps do not have to guess.

What the form asks

Eight short questions, about 45 seconds.

  • Full name and email. Both required.
  • Category. Running Shoes, Casual Shoes or General Items.
  • Product. A dropdown that shows each price.
  • Size. Only the available sizes are offered.
  • Special requests. A free note for the order.
  • Delivery date. A date picker that only allows dates from a set day onward.

What happens next

The thank you screen sets the expectation.

  • Thank you screen. Tells the customer an email with the order details and the invoice is on its way.
  • Behind the scenes. The submission starts the Main Zap.
  • Test data. Screenshots use a test customer.

The Inventory tab. Each size is its own line, and a formula shows Available or Out of Stock. Click to enlarge.

How the stock stays trueA new order takes one off the available stock for that product and size. A cancelled order adds one back. When a line reaches zero, a formula marks it Out of Stock, so the next order for it gets the out of stock email. Every line starts at 20 in this demo.
Step 3 · The order log

Every order in one place, with a colour coded status

The Orders tab is the store's order book. A new row appears the moment a customer submits the form, and the status cell changes colour as staff move the Trello card.

ColumnWhere it comes from
Order Date, Name, EmailFrom the form, written by the Main Zap
Product, Size, PriceFrom the form, with the price cleaned up by a formatter
Notes, Delivery DateFrom the form
Invoice NumberA formula based on the row, in the format NSS-2026-0003
StatusSet by Zaps 4, 5 and 6 when a card is moved: Processing Delivered Cancelled

Step 4 · The invoice

A PDF invoice for every order, with nobody typing it

The Invoice Sub-Zap copies a Google Doc template, fills in the order, exports it as a PDF and emails it to the customer. Each customer gets their own folder in Drive.

The PDF invoice attached to the customer email. Contact details are blurred.

What the Sub-Zap does

  • Checks the customer email is there.
  • Creates a Drive folder for the customer.
  • Copies the invoice template into a new Google Doc.
  • Fills in the product, name, price, notes, total, delivery date and invoice number.
  • Exports a PDF and emails it.
  • If the PDF is missing, the team is alerted in Slack with the order details and told to send it by hand.

The folder created in Drive for the customer.

Step 5 · The human step

One drag moves an order forward

Whether an order is being packed, has arrived or was cancelled is something only a person knows. So the system gives the team a simple Trello board, and one drag of a card does the rest.

1
An order card appearsThe Trello Sub-Zap puts it on the Running Shoes, Casual Shoes or General Order list.
2
Staff move the cardTo Processing, Delivered or Cancelled, as the order progresses.
3
The matching Zap runsIt updates the status in the sheet and emails the customer. A cancelled order also puts its stock back.

The team side, in Slack

One channel for new orders, and a private channel for errors, so problems never get lost in the day to day.

The thinkingTell the customer, tell the team, and never fail silently. Every step that can go wrong has somewhere to report it, so a person can step in only when they are needed.

Step 8 · Beyond the happy path

Edge cases the system handles

A system is only as good as its worst day. These are the situations it was designed for.

SituationWhat happens
The item is out of stockThe customer gets an out of stock email, nothing is deducted and the Zap ends.
A required detail is missingA filter stops the run before anything is logged or sent.
The product cannot be found in the inventoryA filter stops the Zap instead of guessing the stock.
The stock update failsThe team is alerted in a private error channel, and the order does not carry on to the invoice and the board.
The PDF invoice is not createdA Slack alert names the customer, product and invoice number and says what to do by hand.
An item sells outA Slack message tells the team to restock, and the Inventory tab marks the line Out of Stock.
An item has no sizeA formatter handles the missing size, so invoices and emails stay clean for items like the umbrella.
An order is cancelledZap 6 sets the status, emails the customer and adds one back to the stock.
A card has no description, or no emailThe status Zaps stop with a filter instead of sending a broken email.
What I built

The system, in eight pieces

01Order formA Typeform with dropdowns, sizes with prices and a delivery date picker.
02Stock aware Main ZapLogs the order, checks the stock and branches into available or out of stock.
03Inventory and order logOne Google Sheet with an Inventory tab and an Orders tab, both kept up to date by the Zaps.
04Automatic PDF invoicesA Doc template filled in, exported and emailed, with a Drive folder per customer.
05Trello order boardOrders routed by category onto the right list, ready for staff to move.
06Three status ZapsProcessing, Delivered and Cancelled each update the sheet and email the customer.
07Built in error handlingFilters, paths and a private Slack channel catch problems before they reach a customer.
08Customer emails and team alertsFive customer emails and Slack messages for new orders and errors.
Ship it

Build checklist

  • Create the Google Sheet with two tabs: Orders (ten columns, an invoice number formula and a colour coded status) and Inventory (product, category, price, size, stock, available stock and a status formula).
  • Build the Typeform order form: name and email, category, product with price, size, notes, delivery date and a thank you screen.
  • Create the Trello board with six lists: Running Shoes, Casual Shoes, General Order, Processing, Delivered and Cancelled.
  • Design the invoice template in Google Docs and a Drive folder to hold the generated invoices.
  • Set up two Slack channels: one for the team and a private one for errors.
  • Build the Main Zap and its two Sub-Zaps: the invoice, and the Trello path by category.
  • Build the three status Zaps: Processing, Delivered and Cancelled.
  • Add filters and paths so bad data, missing rows and failures stop safely and report to Slack.
  • Test with a test customer: place an order, order an out of stock item, then move a card through each list and check the sheet, the stock and the emails.
The mindset

The sheet is the truth. The Trello card is the status. Staff move one card, and the system does the rest.

One order, one row, and a Zap ready for every step that follows.
